newsitem.title: USA: Dow industrials sink under 8,000, bonds lead way.
newsitem.headline: Dow industrials sink under 8,000, bonds lead way.

text.p: U.S. blue chips continued to drop sharply in afternoon trading on Friday, sinking under the 8,000-point level as bond prices continued their downward spiral and pointed to higher interest rates.
The Dow Jones Industrial average shed 198 points or over two percent to 7989, as the long bond tumbled 1-25/32 to yield 6.66 percent.
The Nasdaq composite shed 30 points to 1594.

"The declines in the bond market are forcing people who had been licking their chops, getting richer and richer, focus on the other side of the market -- the downside," Dick Stein, vice president of U.S. Clearing Corp, said. "When the market comes down, it falls much faster than it ever went up."

Rising bond yields sparked fears of inflation and higher interest rates ahead of key economic data due next week, analysts said. Bonds tumbled amid fears of faster economic growth. They were also hurt by new supply, a weaker dollar, hedge fund selling and technical factors, analysts said.
